title: Edge Offline Inference Adoption Notes
summary: Working notes from the customer discovery and feasibility workshop for running Redwood inference at edge, fully offline (air-gapped) environments. Focused on operator experience, secure artifact transfer, verification tests, and a pragmatic POC acceptance checklist.
body:
Purpose:
These notes capture feasibility observations, operator-runbook proposals, and acceptance criteria for a customer POC that must run Redwood inference in an on-prem, air-gapped edge site. The goal is to surface operational constraints early, propose minimal viable operator procedures, and outline tests that prove the service meets latency, throughput, and security requirements without outbound connectivity.

Scope:
- Target: single-cluster edge site (1-4 GPUs), customer-managed network, no egress to public internet.
- Components in-scope: inference runtime container images, model artifact transfer, KMS/HSM integration (offline key wrap), system monitoring snapshot export, and upgrade/rollback procedures.
- Out-of-scope for this POC: multi-site orchestration, multi-tenant isolation beyond node-level, and long-term telemetry forwarding.

Key constraints discovered in workshop:
- Strict air-gap: customer forbids any direct internet egress from inference subnet.
- Large models (>=7B) require offline physical transfer; single-image size with quantized weights ~6–22 GB depending on quantization.
- HSM available but only via on-prem PKCS#11; no remote KMS allowed.
- Limited ops staff onsite (1 FTE split across 3 projects) — operator steps must be simple and documented.
- Controlled USB media policy: devices must be scanned at a central secure vault before bringing to edge.

Risk scenarios and mitigations:
1) Artifact corruption during physical transfer
   - Risk: model files corrupted or tampered during USB/air-gapped transfer.
   - Mitigation: Provide SHA256 checksums and detached GPG signatures; include step-by-step checksum verification and signature verification commands in runbook.

2) Secrets compromise in local operator machine
   - Risk: operator uses personal laptop to prepare artifacts and keys.
   - Mitigation: Recommend customer-provided staging VM in secured vault; include 'do not use personal devices' policy in runbook.

3) Failure to boot inference container due to kernel or driver mismatch
   - Risk: GPU drivers on edge host mismatch container expectations.
   - Mitigation: Add preflight script to verify kernel, NVIDIA driver version, CUDA/cuDNN compatibility; provide fallback CPU-only container for smoke tests.

Operator runbook (high-level steps):
1) Pre-deployment checklist (remote, before site visit):
   - Confirm target host inventory and remote admin account.
   - Share artifact manifest and transfer process with customer (hashes + signature).
   - Schedule secure media handoff window with customer security team.
2) Media preparation (central secure vault):
   - Build image artifacts in CI with deterministic tags.
   - Create tar.gz of runtime images, model bundle, operator scripts.
   - Generate SHA256 sums and sign with CI's offline key; export signature file.
3) On-site handoff and verification:
   - Customer scans media per policy.
   - Operator copies artifacts to staging host; verify SHA256 and GPG signature.
   - Run preflight.sh: kernel, drivers, disk space (min free 50GB), container runtime presence, GPU availability.
4) Deploy containers with local runtime config:
   - Load images into local registry (or docker load) and start services with systemd unit or k3s manifest.
   - Start model loader and run a cold-start latency test (5 warmup requests, 50 requests for p95).
5) Acceptance smoke tests (detailed below).
6) Post-deployment artifact retention:
   - Leave a copy of checksums and signatures in customer vault.
   - Archive logs and results to encrypted USB handed back to central team.

Pre-deployment checklist (detailed):
- Host inventory: hostname, IP, NIC speed, GPU model, RAM, disk, power redundancy
- Network: internal DNS entries, NTP server, mgmt VLAN for operator laptop, firewall rules for inbound control plane ports only
- Security: list of approved USB devices, contact from customer security, HSM admin account details
- Backup: snapshot schedule and snapshot target (if available)

Acceptance criteria / POC success tests:
- Security: files verified by SHA256 and GPG; keys loaded via PKCS#11 and HSM performs sign/unwrap operations successfully.
- Functionality: end-to-end inference for canonical prompt set returns deterministic structured output within quality tolerance.
- Performance: p95 latency <= X ms (customer target) for baseline model; sustain N qps for 10 minutes without OOM.
- Reliability: service recovers from node reboot within recovery SLA (e.g., 3 minutes).
- Operability: operator can perform an upgrade and rollback using runbook steps with < 30 minutes downtime.

On-site validation tests (examples):
- Check GPU visibility: nvidia-smi and sample CUDA program run.
- Container smoke: docker load image -> docker run hello-infer to validate dependencies.
- Model checksum and signature verification test: deliberate tamper negative test to validate detection.
- Latency run: 1000 sequential single-request measurements and compute p50/p95.

Monitoring & telemetry plan for air-gapped sites:
- Local: runprom (lightweight Prometheus) + node exporter, pushgateway not allowed.
- Export strategy: nightly log/metric snapshot tar.gz pushed to encrypted USB, signed and cataloged; sent to central analytics via secure courier.
- Alerting: SMS or pager via customer's on-prem alerting; if not available, operator-notify script that emails to pre-approved address through internal mail relay.

Security notes (KMS/HSM):
- Use PKCS#11 module for key operations. Provide sample integration snippet for runtime to call HSM for unwrapping model encryption keys.
- Key wrapping: models encrypted at rest with customer-wrapped key; runtime receives wrapped key and asks HSM to unwrap locally.
- No plaintext keys leave the site.

Upgrade and rollback strategy:
- Blue/green not possible for single small cluster; recommend staged rolling upgrade: pull new images to staging, stop inference, swap containers, run smoke tests, if failure revert to previous image.
- Keep last two models and last two runtime images cached on host for fast rollback.

Minimal target hardware profile (recommendation):
- CPU: 8 cores (2.4GHz+)
- RAM: 64GB
- GPU: 1xA10G or equivalent with 24GB GPU RAM (or at least 16GB for smaller models)
- Disk: 1TB NVMe (prefer RAID for redundancy)
- Network: 1Gbps internal fabric

Artifact packaging & size guidance:
- Model bundles: tar.gz + signature. Include metadata file with tokenizer, vocab, expected input shape, sample prompts. Keep bundle < 25GB where possible.
- Container images: prefer multi-arch slim images; provide compressed tar layers for offline load.

Performance trade-offs and recommendations:
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization reduces model size significantly but requires careful evaluation of downstream quality. Recommend quant Q4_HYBRID for latency-sensitive edge POCs.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for throughput gains; include cache warmup plan in runbook to avoid first-request latency spikes.

Customer readiness questionnaire (to send pre-visit):
- Do you have an HSM or on-prem KMS? If yes, vendor and connectivity?
- List of approved USB device serials or policy contact.
- Onsite contact and escalation chain with phone numbers.
- Maintenance window preferences and blackout dates.
- Host inventory sheet (see attached template).

Proposed POC timeline (2-week micro-POC):
- Day -7: Confirm inventory, schedule courier, prepare artifacts and signatures.
- Day 0: Secure media handoff and on-site operator verification.
- Day 1: Preflight and container bootstrap, run smoke tests.
- Day 2: Performance runs and acceptance tests.
- Day 3: Operator training and upgrade/rollback drill.
- Day 4–7: Stabilization and additional regression tests; central team collects archived snapshots.

Open questions (workshop unresolved):
- Customer policy on USB invention frequency: how often can we bring new media?
- Is there an approved air-gapped continuous integration path, or will all artifacts be hand-built per release?
- Can we leverage internal registry appliance at customer to avoid repeated docker load operations?

Action items (owners):
- Asha: finalize preflight.sh and attach to runbook (due 2025-11-21).
- Michael: create CI job to produce signed model bundles for POC (ENG-4523) (due 2025-11-14).
- Irene: draft operator quickstart one-pager and training checklist (due 2025-11-20).
- Diego: confirm HSM integration example and test vectors (due 2025-11-18).

Appendix: useful commands and snippets (to be expanded in runbook):
- Verify checksum: sha256sum model.tar.gz | tee model.sha256
- Verify signature: gpg --verify model.tar.gz.sig model.tar.gz
- PKCS#11 test: pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/libmypkcs11.so -O
- Preflight: ./preflight.sh --expect-gpu --min-disk-gb 50

Notes to self:
- Keep runbook terse (one page checklists + one expanded troubleshooting page).
- Prepare a minimal 'rescue' USB with CPU-only container and smoke tests in case GPU runtime fails.

References:
- See linked artifacts for PR and Confluence playbook draft.

Status: draft — want to review with customer security and SRE before finalizing into formal POC runbook.
